base_member_text: [L5-L7] (MED/working-directory/contract) The script assumes it starts in a directory whose parent contains `trunk/`; it does not anchor paths to the script location or check either `cd`, so invocation from another directory changes the build target.

[L22-L35] (MED/error-handling/reproducibility) Cleanup, generation, configure, build, install, and artifact creation have no failure checks or `set -e`, so stale or partial artifacts can be published after an earlier failure.
audit_member_text: [L5-L39] (HIGH/build-failure-propagation) The script never stops on failed directory changes, module loads, configuration, compilation or installation, allowing stale binaries to be packaged and a later successful command to mask the failed build.

adversarial.rationale: trunk/config/teamcity-build.sh:5-39 never checks the directory changes or build/install results, retains the existing installation prefix, and archives that same prefix at lines 33-35. The backup at line 19 does not clean the live installation, and no source-tree caller establishes errexit, so failed builds can leave old installed binaries available for packaging while a successful final module-generation command supplies a zero script status.

base_member_text: [L19] (MED/error-handling/path) The unconditional recursive copy of the prior installation has no existence check or failure handling, and with no `set -e` a missing prior installation does not stop the publication pipeline.

[L28] (LOW/flags/contract) The configure invocation places curl library/include flags in FCFLAGS, including a `bin` directory as an include path, leaving the Fortran/compiler flag contract suspicious and toolchain-dependent.

audit_member_text: [L19] (MED/backup-semantics) Repeated cp -r into an existing _prev directory nests the current installation beneath it instead of replacing the previous snapshot.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: L19 uses cp -r with a fixed previous-installation destination and never removes that destination or requests replacement semantics. Once that destination directory exists, cp places the source directory beneath it, leaving the earlier snapshot at the destination root.
